Monthly housing market data for Texas MLS areas, 2000-2015

tx_housing_markets.Rd

A cleaned version of ggplot2::txhousing, with one row per market area per month, plus inflation-adjusted median prices. Used to explore how Texas housing markets changed before, during and after the 2008 financial crisis.

Usage

tx_housing_markets

Format

A tibble with 8,602 rows and 11 columns:

area

Multiple listing service (MLS) area. Most are cities, but some are counties or regions, such as Collin County or Bay Area.

date

The month the figures refer to, stored as the first day of that month.

year

Year.

month

Month, from 1 (January) to 12 (December).

period

Phase of the housing cycle: Pre-crisis (2000-2006), Downturn (2007-2010) or Recovery (2011-2015). The cut-offs follow total sales across all 46 areas, which peaked in 2006 and were lowest in 2010.

sales

Number of homes sold.

volume

Total value of sales, in US dollars.

median

Median sale price, in US dollars, as reported at the time (not adjusted for inflation).

median_real

Median sale price adjusted for inflation, in July 2015 US dollars, using the Consumer Price Index for the US South region.

listings

Total active listings.

inventory

Months inventory: the time it would take to sell all current listings at the current pace of sales.

Source

Housing data: originally collected by the Texas A&M University (TAMU) Real Estate Center, https://trerc.tamu.edu/. This package uses the copy distributed in the ggplot2 package as ggplot2::txhousing.

Inflation data: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items in South (CUUR0300SA0), retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CUUR0300SA0.

Details

The data run from January 2000 to July 2015, so 2015 is a partial year. median_real converts each month's median price to July 2015 dollars, so prices from different years can be compared fairly. It uses the CPI for the US South region, which includes Texas, because no monthly CPI is published for Texas alone. Some areas have missing values, particularly for listings and inventory; these are kept as NA rather than removed. The script used to prepare the data is data-raw/tx_housing_markets.R in the package source.
